problems: The blind guess (a standing person with outstretched arms) does not match the intended subject, a fid. The drawing reads as a T-shaped tool with a splayed bottom, not a figure. The title 'Ruskel — the Fid' confirms the intent.
The figure is upright: knob at top, spike point at bottom, which is correct for a fid.
Star 37826 (the bright knot where handle meets spike) sits on the junction just below the knob, which is right.
Star 37740 (waist of spike shaft) sits on the shaft, and star 37908 (spike point) sits at the splayed strand origin, both correct.

Grip bar ends: the left end star sits at the left end of the bar, but the label text for left and right ends overlaps and is illegible ('left end of the grip bar' runs into 'right end of the grip bar').
The right-end grip star is ambiguous: a nearby background star at about (336,181) sits near the label, so the reader may confuse it with the bar end.
The crown-of-knob label points to a small star at the top edge of the knob, which is roughly right, but the knob is tiny and the label text collides with the knot label.
Labels are cluttered and overlap each other and background stars (e.g. 'the waist of the spike shaft' runs across an unrelated background star), which hurts legibility.

Silhouette: the blue outlines around the shaft, grip bar, and splayed strands give some body to the figure, but the gold lines dominate, so the form still reads as a skeleton trace more than a solid silhouette.
The knob is only a small blue loop, so the fid's bulbous wooden crown is underplayed.
output.advice: Redraw so the silhouette carries the shape: make the fid a solid tapered spike (wide at the handle, narrowing to a point at bottom) with a visibly larger wooden knob at top. Keep the grip bar as a clear cross-bar. Place stars: 37629 on the top edge of the knob, 37826 at the knob-to-spike junction, 37740 on the shaft waist, 37908 at the spike tip where the strands split, and 38538 and 36962 at the two ends of the grip bar. Move the labels so they do not overlap each other or the background stars, e.g. put the two grip-bar labels on opposite sides (left label to the left, right label to the right) and stagger the rest. Keep the figure upright (knob top, point bottom). Reduce the gold-line weight so the blue silhouette reads as the main form.
